title: Known-answer Schwarzschild exterior tensor benchmark
capability_added: Verify one position-dependent curved metric through symbolic derivatives, connection, curvature, vacuum tensors, and a curvature invariant.

excluded_sets: theta = 0 and theta = pi spherical-coordinate axis degeneracy
domain.chart_coverage: Exterior curvature-coordinate patch only; no claim about a horizon-penetrating or maximal extension.

conventions.riemann_tensor_definition: R^rho_{sigma mu nu} = d_mu Gamma^rho_{nu sigma} - d_nu Gamma^rho_{mu sigma} + Gamma^rho_{mu lambda} Gamma^lambda_{nu sigma} - Gamma^rho_{nu lambda} Gamma^lambda_{mu sigma}

expected_results.stress_energy: all zero in the exterior vacuum domain

negative_cases.case: Change the time-time metric coefficient sign or mass factor.
Declare M <= 0 or allow r <= 2*M in the evaluated chart.
Remove the sin(theta)**2 factor from g_phi_phi.
Perturb the radial metric inverse factor.
Flip the declared Riemann convention without transforming expected components.
Report every Riemann component as zero.
Introduce a nonzero Ricci or Einstein component in the exterior.
Replace the curvature invariant with a constant or zero.
Evaluate theta at a spherical-coordinate axis while claiming the chart is nonsingular there.

unsupported_properties: The Schwarzschild interior, horizon-penetrating charts, or maximal extension
Matter-source reconstruction inside the central body
Geodesic integration, orbit stability, travel time, or tidal-force safety
Perturbative or nonlinear stability of the spacetime
Numerical relativity, dynamical collapse, rotation, or charge
Any novel geometry, device, engineering, or transportation claim

references.title: On the Gravitational Field of a Mass Point According to Einstein's Theory
Lectures on General Relativity
references.purpose: Metric, vacuum equation, exterior domain, horizon, and singularity conventions.
